Good point. Having a successful post on reddit basically just means you randomly got lucky, or have the timing/repost/on some mod's good side thing down to a science. Here, it means you said or submitted something relevant and interesting.

There is a formula to it. It shouldn't take you long to figure out what kinds of posts get upvoted and which ones don't.

So you browse /new/ and pick those out. And you plant one of the first comments on a topic that you know will get the votes "we need to get rid of the career politicians and take the money put of the too-big-to-jail banks" blah blah.

The post gains momentum and you are the #1 honeypot comment. I went from about 1000 comment karma to 50,000 in a week or two.

For link karma you mostly play the numbers game - just find a fresh article or two and post it in any sub where it might fit. The niche subs are the best cause they're guaranteed karma.

You can also "cherrypick" for link karma. Look in /new/ for an article that will likely take off, and whore it out to fringe subs. Something on /r/politics saying Hillary did something bad? Throw it into /r/conservative and /r/libertarian

There's also what I call "dupe-whoring" - you find something on maybe /r/news from ABC saying "*Plane Crash Kills ___*". Find the same story on NBC and Fox then post it in the same subs - after all, you already know it's going to be a successful story.

At some point after I had all this figured out and working for me, I'd realized all I was doing was expending valuable mental energy on imaginary Internet points and that I could never cash them in.
